chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the woman whose husband divorces her while she is menstruating once every three months, he (peace be upon him) said: 'When three months have passed, her waiting period is fulfilled. Each month is counted for her as a menstruation.'
ai.seo_question: How is the waiting period calculated for a woman who menstruates once every three months?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'iddah for a woman with irregular menstruation (حَيْضَة) who experiences a cycle only once every three months, ruling that her waiting period is three months, with each month counted as one cycle. This establishes a practical legal mechanism for calculating purity intervals when the standard monthly rhythm is absent, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on adapting ritual law to biological reality. The ruling ensures that the woman is not unduly prolonged in a state of uncertainty, balancing legal precision with ease for the individual.
